texto:
Roblox chief executive David Baszucki told analysts on October 29, 2026 that artificial intelligence has set off "a massive surge in creation velocity" on the platform, and that its advertising system has reached "an inflection point" because more developers are paying to buy traffic. The remarks, made on the company's third-quarter earnings call, describe a shift that reaches well beyond one gaming platform. When the cost of making content falls sharply, the scarce resource becomes distribution - and distribution is sold by whoever owns the recommendation engine and the ad slots.
The call followed the release of Roblox's third-quarter results that afternoon. Quotes in this article come from a transcript of the call published by Investing.com on October 30, which the outlet says was generated with the support of AI and reviewed by an editor.
The supply figures Baszucki gave were steep. More than 80% of the top 100 games ranked by hours used AI in their creation over the past month. Two titles created almost exclusively with AI reached the top 20 by concurrent players during the third quarter. Daily asset uploads to Roblox's cloud tripled from one month to the next, and daily users of the company's MCP server grew nearly fivefold from the second quarter. Roblox shares fell 16.98% to $43.55 in after-hours trading, according to Investing.com, which tied the move to weaker fourth-quarter bookings guidance.
In Short
Roblox's boss said AI tools now let almost anyone make a game quickly, so the number of games on the platform is shooting up. With so many new games fighting for the same players, more of the people who make them are paying Roblox for ads so their games get noticed. That turns Roblox's recommendations and its ad slots into the main route to an audience, and the same pattern is showing up wherever AI makes content cheap to produce.
"An inflection point" in the ad system
Baszucki's remark came at the end of a run of AI statistics in his prepared comments. "There's also an inflection point going on in our ad system as more devs are using ads to buy traffic," he said. He gave no count of advertisers, no spend figure and no growth rate for that buying, and Roblox does not report advertising revenue as a separate line.
The connection between AI creation and ad demand became clearer in the question-and-answer session. Chris Schoell of UBS asked how Roblox would hold on to developers as new AI-powered creation platforms emerge. Baszucki's answer linked the rise in AI tool usage directly to the ad system. "Part of the reason we are seeing so much MCP usage and tagging into our ad system is when people build games, they are looking for a way to get them distributed, either through our RFY algorithm, as well as a place to run them, especially if they are multiplayer," he said. RFY refers to Recommended for You, the personalized surface on the Roblox home page.
MCP, short for Model Context Protocol, is the route through which creators plug outside AI systems into Roblox Studio. Baszucki described it as the way people connect their own external frontier models to Roblox. In other words, the creators who rely most heavily on third-party AI to build games are, by his account, also among those reaching for paid distribution.
Matt Cost of Morgan Stanley asked when faster creation would show up in user and bookings growth. Baszucki pointed to Build, the company's prompt-based creation tool. "We are seeing right now, games created with Build start to monetize, and we're seeing people buying ads with that. We're in the middle of it," he said. Build has been tested with more than 500,000 users in New Zealand, Singapore, Serbia and Thailand, who have published more than 70,000 games. "We already see multiple titles running ads and making money, and the vast majority of Build users have never previously opened Roblox Studio," Baszucki said. A broader US release is scheduled for December 2026, with a global rollout in 2027.
The sequence Baszucki described runs in one direction. AI lowers the cost of building a game. New builders, most of whom have never used the professional toolset, publish more games. Those games need players. The ad system sells access to players. For Roblox, each step feeds the next.
What "running sponsored ads" covers
Baszucki also restated the platform's ad formats. "Our sponsor tiles and rewarded video products are demonstrating really expanding product market fit, with over 70% of the top 100 games running sponsored ads," he said.
That figure still leaves a gap. Roblox sells sponsored placements both to creators promoting their own games and to brands, and the call did not separate the two. Nor did either executive say whether "running" means buying promotion or carrying ad units. Baszucki's "inflection point" comment, by contrast, was explicit: it was about developers buying traffic.
How fast AI content is arriving
Baszucki opened the call with a statement about the wider industry rather than Roblox alone. "We've seen just in the last few weeks or month, really reverse engineering of all standalone code has become very commonplace," he said. Both open-source and frontier models continue to gain capability, according to Baszucki, and "the time required to go from an idea to a playable game is compressing dramatically."
The statistics he offered to back that claim were as follows:
Baszucki treats asset uploads as the cleanest signal. "We think assets with our images, textures, meshes, are a good proxy for the amount of creativity that's going on," he said. Later, answering Morgan Stanley, he added that "a lot of those are AI-generated textures, meshes, assets." On the two hits: "A year ago, I do not think we would have imagined that we would have 2 of the top 20 experiences on Roblox primarily AI generated."
The volume was already large before this quarter. When SuperAwesome became Roblox's only third-party partner for under-13 advertising in June 2026, it said about 15,000 new games were being uploaded to Roblox daily. Roblox did not give an updated daily figure on the call.
The tooling behind Build is, in Baszucki's description, a router rather than a single model. "Our harness right now is routing prompts across multiple models, both for code, for 3D scene gen, for audio. Avatar models are coming online and more," he said. The same harness powers Roblox Studio Assistant, the tool used by professional developers.
Roblox is not the only company pushing AI game creation at consumers. Google opened Playground, its AI game creation tool, to US adults on October 7, 2026, with creation access tied to Google's AI subscription tiers.
Ranking for retention, not this quarter's revenue
If AI multiplies supply, the recommendation algorithm decides which games get seen without paying. Bryan Smilek of JPMorgan framed his question around that choice, noting that Roblox had decided "to more effectively balance LTV and monetization with an algorithm." LTV is the lifetime value of a user.
Baszucki described a system tuned for long-run behavior. "We are driving direct measurements and optimization of long-term retention," he said. According to Baszucki, "the algo is pushing more dynamic content to the surface while simultaneously bringing long-term retention high." Then came the line most relevant to any platform facing a flood of machine-made content: "We are also on our way with algo improvements that I think will take advantage of more creativity with AI rather than succumb to it. Even as we see more content being pushed to our platform, we are designing with that in mind to find the great new content within arguably more content."
Recommended for You is a recommender system, and Roblox says it now feeds it more signals than before. "In Q3, we've more and more incorporated age cohorts and play data into our recommendation algorithm," Baszucki said. He reported that 40% of the weekly top 100 Recommended for You games by impressions were created within the previous three months. Chief financial officer Naveen Chopra gave a broader version of the same measure: "In Q3, 40% of the top 1,000 games by hours launched in the last 90 days."
Chopra credited the algorithm with part of the quarter's retention, which reached its highest seasonally adjusted level since 2021. The optimization, he said, helped new titles, among them Steal an Egg, build large audiences quickly. He was also direct about what that approach costs in the short run. "As expected, monetization headwinds did continue in the quarter, particularly with younger cohorts in the U.S. But we remain confident that the RFY-driven lift we are observing to engagement and retention translates to higher user LTV over time," he said. For fourth-quarter guidance, he added, "we do not assume short-term improvement in monetization."
That is a choice other platforms have handled differently. YouTube, faced with mass-produced uploads, adjusted monetization eligibility instead: it renamed its "repetitious content" guideline "inauthentic content" on July 15, 2025, while saying AI tools used for storytelling do not affect eligibility. Roblox's executives, on this call at least, put the weight on ranking.
Roblox as an advertiser: the ROAS bar
Roblox is also a buyer of media. Chopra said the company would keep raising spend aimed at adults. "We also plan to continue to increase marketing spend targeting over 18 users. We have been encouraged by what we have seen as we have been dialing up this type of spend," he said.
His justification is one that performance marketers will recognize. "Retention, engagement, and monetization of paid users is outperforming organic sign-ups, which means it is a very efficient way for us to jumpstart the flywheel for 18 and over users. We plan to continue scaling while also maintaining a high ROAS bar," Chopra said. He gave no ROAS threshold, named no channels and did not say how the paid and organic cohorts were compared.
The adult cohort is where Roblox sees the money. In the US, daily active users aged 18 and over grew 18% year over year and 89% over two years, according to Baszucki, and "our 18 and up users monetize 50% or more than our under 18 cohort."
Pre-roll: a test in "select cohorts and countries"
The one new detail on ad inventory came in a single sentence. "We expect to be testing skippable pre-roll video ads in select cohorts and countries, with expanding first-party inventory this year," Baszucki said. The shareholder letter released the same day described the plan without dates or markets. The call narrows it to a test, though the sentence leaves unclear whether "this year" applies to the test or to the inventory expansion, and only two months of 2026 remain.
First-party inventory matters because much of Roblox's existing ad supply is placed by creators inside their own games. Third parties sell parts of it. Magnite took exclusive global programmatic rights to Roblox's mobile rewarded video inventory, announced on January 6, 2026, and on the July 31, 2025 earnings call Roblox said nearly 100 publishers had joined its Google-integrated rewarded video product. Neither partner came up on this call. Neither did the advertiser metrics Roblox published in February, when its fourth-quarter 2025 letter reported rewarded video completion rates above 90% and viewability of 95% across more than 1,000 brands.
Data as the moat
Baszucki's answer to the competition question rested on proprietary data. "We have over 20 years of data now on the platform, and we get over 350 million hours of daily data. This is powering now over 400 internal proprietary models that we fine-tuned on top of open weights in some cases," he said. Roblox reported 33.8 billion engagement hours for the quarter; spread over its 92 days, that works out to about 367 million hours a day, a PPC Land calculation consistent with his figure.
Two of the uses he named carry over directly to commerce and advertising. "Our discovery models are trained on billions of daily signals right now, and our economy models more and more are optimizing pricing and storefront placement," he said. Pricing and placement optimization inside a virtual economy is the same class of problem retail media networks and marketplaces work on.
He returned to the point when asked about rival platforms. "The way we power our discovery systems, our safety systems, our AI harness, our economy, is all based on the historic proprietary data we have gathered on the platform. Those systems get better and better the more data we get, and we are continuing to improve those models," Baszucki said.
Safety is one of those systems. Roblox is moving to capture what Baszucki called "4D telemetry," which he defined as "location and time, all the way down to the instance and frame level." The aim is moderation that "evaluates entire 3D scenes." As an example, he said Roblox now evaluates avatars "in the combinations of clothing," a check that runs automatically within its moderation system.
Age checks: "foreshadowing where the industry is going"
Andrew Marok of Raymond James asked about chat density, which took a hit when Roblox rolled out age checks globally, and whether part of that effect might be structural. Baszucki began with coverage. "We've shared a bit that over 80% of our daily users, 13 through 17 U.S.A., have age checked," he said. By Roblox's estimate, 30% of all US 13- to 17-year-olds use the platform daily.
He then made an industry-wide claim. "I believe what we're doing is really foreshadowing where the industry is going, and we're really proud of the work we've done. We see other companies following in the direction we've put out," Baszucki said. He did not name the companies.
On chat itself, the data point was sequential. "Our chat DAUs are up 24% quarter-on-quarter. As we age check more, we are seeing more chat activity," he said. The answer did not address the second half of the question: whether chat density has returned to pre-check levels. Earlier this year the coverage was far lower. Through January 31, 2026, 45% of Roblox's 144 million daily users had completed age verification.
Distribution beyond the Roblox app
Several of the initiatives Baszucki described would push Roblox games into channels that marketers already buy.
Roblox Everywhere would put Roblox games into third-party app stores as standalone apps. In phase one, which Roblox estimates will launch in the first half of 2027, the company will itself curate and publish select top titles. In phase two, any creator would be able to generate a standalone binary in the creator portal and submit it to the app store of their choice. Baszucki illustrated it with an app store search. "The way to think about this is imagine going to search for Grow a Garden in your favorite app store and finding both a standalone game, called Grow a Garden, as well as that game being available on the Roblox app at the same time," he said. He summed up the approach as "build once, publish everywhere." The call did not cover how the standalone apps would be monetized, which store fees would apply, or who would pay for app store promotion.
Browser play is the second route. Roblox is now targeting WebAssembly with the same engine, which Baszucki said should "enable instant one-click browser play initially in Google Chrome." He described it as "Roblox without a download." No date was given.
Universal Player runs the other way, bringing outside games in. Roblox is developing "an AI-supported system, which is going to allow creators to import literally any existing PC, console, or mobile game directly onto the platform," according to Baszucki. Imported games would gain what he calls "Robloxification": multiplayer, instant joining without a download, cross-device play and frequent updates. Creators would have a game working "in a matter of days rather than weeks or a month," he said, and later, for major studios, "not in months, but in a day."
James Heaney of Jefferies asked whether that would require licenses from the owners of the games being ported. "We really respect IP and respect DMCA takedown. We want licensed IP on our platform," Baszucki said. He did not say whether a license would be a condition of importing a game. He did describe Roblox's IP manager, where studios can place content for other creators to use under license.
Roblox Reality, scheduled for early access in the first half of 2027, "couples generative video world models to move towards really the dream of multiplayer photorealism," Baszucki said. Google is working on the same class of model: it presented Genie 4 as a research preview for trusted testers on October 27, 2026.
The bill for inference
All of this costs compute, and the part that grows with use is inference, the running of trained models to answer prompts. "We are going to be adding more compute, more GPU as we look forward to, for example, Build, which has some inference, but we are being very thoughtful of it right now," Baszucki said. "Part of our secret sauce to date has been just running infra very efficiently. We are not going to lose track of that."
Chopra said infrastructure expense would rise in the fourth quarter and grow again year over year in 2027, without giving figures. He described a change in the shape of those costs. "A lot of the investments we are making in infra now take more of the form of fixed expense as opposed to variable, because a lot of it is related to model training," he said. Roblox likes that for two reasons, according to Chopra: more of the work can move on-premises over time, and fixed costs become a source of operating leverage as revenue grows. Build's wider release in December will add to the inference load.
The capital numbers are specific. About $140 million of capital expenditure shifted from the third quarter into the fourth. Roblox plans $380 million of capital spending in the fourth quarter, implying $468 million for 2026, which Chopra said sits at the low end of the range the company gave at the start of the year.
The balance sheet gives Roblox room. Chopra said the company holds about $5 billion of net cash. "Having a lot of dry powder there, I think is an important thing, particularly given the speed at which the AI landscape is changing, and we never want to be in a position where we can't invest as quickly and aggressively as we think is prudent," he said. Roblox has made "tuck-in type acquisitions" to bring in AI talent and wants the option to "do bigger things," Chopra said. Over the last couple of quarters it bought back "probably over $400 million worth of stock" under a $3 billion authorization.
Guidance, GTA and the share price
Roblox expects fourth-quarter bookings to fall 10% to 15% from a year earlier. Chopra said the guidance does not assume that recent strength from hit games and Halloween events will repeat, and that the midpoint implies annualized growth of 26% over two years.
The guidance includes what Chopra called "some modest headwinds" from the release of Grand Theft Auto during the quarter, though he conceded the size is uncertain. "There really is not a lot of data or analogous releases by which to try to estimate the impact that GTA may have. It is a pretty different demo than what we have on the platform today," he said. "It is a console-only release." Baszucki offered a different reading of big launches: "When we have cultural moments, people do lean into cultural moments on Roblox as well and similar types of genres."
Shares closed the regular session at $52.46, down 1.54%, before the after-hours fall to $43.55, according to Investing.com, which put the stock's 52-week range at $33.88 to $126.28. Investing.com reported an adjusted loss of $0.32 a share against an expected loss of $0.43. Its summary also gave revenue of $1.7 billion against a $1.64 billion forecast. Roblox's own reported figures were revenue of $1.572 billion and bookings of $1.697 billion, so the $1.7 billion figure matches bookings, not revenue.
The call ended with a brand moment. Baszucki invited listeners to watch the Jonas Brothers appear inside Steal an Egg, one of the platform's trending games, on October 31 at 8:00 a.m. Pacific.
Why this matters for the marketing industry
Roblox is an unusually clear case of a pattern visible across digital media, because it owns every stage: the AI tools that make the content, the recommendation system that ranks it and the ad system that sells reach. On this call, its chief executive tied the first stage to the third in plain terms. More creation leads to more developers buying traffic.
The same link is appearing elsewhere. AI app builders have started wiring commercial plumbing into their tools: Replit integrated RevenueCat on April 9, 2026 so that apps built by prompt could take payments, and Base44 added Google Ads Performance Max campaign management inside its chat builder in September 2026. Gaming platforms are opening ad buying to smaller studios too. Discord introduced Ads Manager on September 29, 2026, with fully self-serve access planned for early 2027. Beyond any single platform, the market for paid app user acquisition is already large: AppLovin reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of $1.92 billion, up 53%.
Quality is the other side of the volume. PPC Land has tracked how creator payment programs fuel the spread of low-quality AI content across social platforms and why advertisers have reason to care about AI slop. Roblox's executives claim their algorithm can "take advantage of more creativity with AI rather than succumb to it." The evidence they offered is that newer games are reaching the top charts and that retention is at its highest seasonally adjusted level since 2021. They offered no measure of how much low-quality content the system filters out, or of how many AI-built games get no players at all.
For advertisers buying on Roblox, more games could mean more places to run rewarded video and more creators selling inventory. It also means more creators competing for the same home page placements as brand-built games. The planned pre-roll test points the other way, toward inventory Roblox controls directly.
One question went unasked on the call. When the same company runs both the algorithm that hands out free reach and the ad system that sells paid reach, how will creators tell which one is delivering their players? Roblox has not published data that would answer it.

Summary
Who: Roblox Corporation, its co-founder and chief executive David Baszucki and its chief financial officer Naveen Chopra, answering analysts from JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Morgan Stanley, Jefferies, UBS, Raymond James, Citi, Macquarie and Oppenheimer.
What: Baszucki said an "inflection point" is under way in Roblox's ad system as more developers buy traffic, linking it to a surge in AI-built games: more than 80% of the top 100 games used AI in creation in the past month, two almost entirely AI-made titles reached the top 20, and asset uploads tripled. Chopra said Roblox itself is raising paid marketing to adults under "a high ROAS bar," and Baszucki said skippable pre-roll ads will be tested in select cohorts and countries.
When: The third-quarter 2026 earnings call took place on October 29, 2026. Investing.com published its transcript on October 30.
Where: On Roblox's platform worldwide, with Build tests in New Zealand, Singapore, Serbia and Thailand, a broader US Build release in December 2026, and plans to reach third-party app stores and the Chrome browser.
Why: AI is cutting the cost of making games, which raises the number of titles competing for the same players. That shifts value toward recommendation and paid distribution, which Roblox controls, and it previews a pattern that applies to any platform where AI makes content cheap to produce.
